target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of leaf base (PO_0020040)
reason: Moss descriptions of the cells at the base of the phyllid (PO_0020040 has 'phyllid base' as a synonym). Use the cell class with part_of leaf base, like laminal cell FLOPO_0986100 and supra-alar cell FLOPO_0986088. The record should also carry non-vascular leaf PO_0025075.

target: gametophore branch (PO_0030021)
reason: Narrower: in mosses and liverworts, a slender whip-like branch with reduced leaves; the µm diameters 'including leaves' show bryophytes. The flagelliform shape can be stated as a quality of the gametophore branch.

target: floral disc (FLOPO_0986025) part of pistillate flower (PO_0025599), pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole)
reason: The disc of the female flowers ('hypogyne', pubescent or glabrous). This is 'calyx of male flowers' with the sex qualifying the whole flower, not the disc.

target: phyllome lamina tooth (PO_0025515)
reason: Narrower: a serrature is one tooth of a serrate margin. Phyllome lamina tooth covers leaves, leaflets and bracts. Use leaf lamina tooth PO_0025518 when the organ is known to be a leaf.

target: branch (PO_0025073) with bearer state young (PATO_0000309), pattern 04
reason: The state of the bearer: 'young' is already a bearer_quality context word (PATO_0000309). Twig and branchlet are already synonyms of branch.

target: fruit distal end (PO_0008001)
reason: Exact: PO defines it as the end of a fruit distal from the fruit pedicel, which is the apex that floras describe as acute, obtuse or apiculate.

target: phyllome lamina (PO_0025396) part of keel petal (PO_0025326)
reason: The blade of a clawed keel petal of papilionoid legumes, as opposed to its claw. It is falcate and auriculate at the base, and its widths belong to the blade.

target: inflorescence (PO_0009049)
reason: Narrower: in Troll and Weberling's terms, the whole flowering system of a shoot made up of several partial inflorescences. PO's inflorescence already covers compound systems of flowers and inflorescence axes. Counts such as '3-5 synflorescences' are counts of inflorescences.

label: elaiophore
parent: is_a portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656); part_of flower (PO_0009046)
definition: A portion of secretory tissue (PO:0005656) of a flower (PO:0009046) that secretes non-volatile oils collected by pollinators, either as a glandular area of trichomes (trichomal elaiophore) or as a gland covered by a secretory epidermis (epithelial elaiophore), as on the calyx of Malpighiaceae and Krameria and the labellum of some orchids. NOTE: Distinct from oil gland PO:0005669, which is an internal oil cavity, and from flower nectary PO:0009056. Propose to PO upstream.
reason: A real and widespread floral structure (Malpighiaceae calyx glands, Krameriaceae, Iridaceae, Orchidaceae) with no class in PO. Modelled on colleter FLOPO_0986023. The examples use it for presence, colour and shape.

target: spine shield (FLOPO_0986078)
reason: Exact: the class exists, and its label or plural only lacks a bearer rule (Euphorbia spine shields).

target: whole plant (PO_0000003)
reason: Exact: the examples are sexual systems (dioecious, monoecious, autoicous, synoicous) that inhere in the whole plant. 'male/female plant' is already handled as a context word.

target: phyllome margin (PO_0025018) part of perichaetal bract (PO_0030030)
reason: Perichaetial leaves are PO's perichaetal bracts, so 'perichaetial leaf' should be a lexicon synonym of PO_0030030. The margin is a region of that bract.

target: trichome (PO_0000282, synonym 'scale') part of petiole (PO_0020038)
reason: Scales on the petiole or stipe (mostly ferns), described as linear, lanceolate, ciliate or tangled. PO treats scales as trichomes, and the patterns can express a trichome that is part of a named organ.

target: connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073)
reason: Exact synonym of the existing FLOPO class (Melastomataceae and others).

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656, 'gland') part of leaf (PO_0025034)
reason: The earlier review mapped 'gland' to PO_0005656. Use extrafloral nectary PO_0009057 only when the flora says the gland secretes nectar.

target: margin region of seed (PO_0009010) through the region pattern; seed wing (FLOPO_0986091) when described as winglike
reason: A region of the seed, so a margin of an existing class. A winglike, broadened margin is the seed wing, which already exists.

target: leaflet margin (PO_0006034)
reason: Narrower: PO lists pinna as a synonym of leaflet, so the margin of a pinna is a leaflet margin. This covers cycad and fern pinnae; for ferns, also give pinna FLOPO_0985027 on the record.

target: peduncle (PO_0009053)
reason: Exact: a peduncle is the stalk of an inflorescence, and PO lists 'inflorescence stem' as a synonym.

target: calyx (PO_0009060) at fruit development stage (PO_0001002), pattern 04
reason: The persistent calyx in the fruiting state. 'fruiting' is already a stage context word mapping to PO_0001002.

target: locule (PO_0025263)
reason: Narrower: a locellus is a small secondary compartment, usually of a septate anther. Without the organ, the generic locule class is the safe target; use anther locule PO_0025264 when the statement is about stamens. Only counts occur.

target: flower pedicel (PO_0030113) part of staminate flower (PO_0025600), pattern 12
reason: The same as 'calyx of male flowers': the sex qualifies the flower, and the pedicel is its part.

label: perennating organ
definition: A plant organ (PO:0009008) that persists through an unfavourable season, by which the plant survives and from which new growth arises, such as a tuber, corm, pseudobulb or rhizome. NOTE: A functional grouping class kept in FLOPO for floras (e.g. Orchidaceae: 'perennating organs subterranean, tuberous') that do not say which organ it is; not to be proposed to PO, which classifies organs by structure.
reason: Used in at least two floras for subterranean tubers, corms or pseudobulbs whose type is not stated. No single PO class covers it, and mapping to a specific one (tuber PO_0025522, corm PO_0025355) would be wrong. Low confidence: a FLOPO union class (tuber or corm or rhizome or pseudobulb) would do the same job, or the word could be rejected.

target: stem (PO_0009047) with position aerial (pattern 18) at flowering stage (PO_0007616, pattern 04)
reason: A state and a position of an existing class. 'flowering' is already a stage context word. Counts ('usually 1') are counts of stems.

target: cypsela (FLOPO_0986053), the body as distinct from carpopodium (FLOPO_0986132) and fruit beak (FLOPO_0986139)
reason: In Asteraceae (carpopodium, beak) the body is the cypsela without its beak and carpopodium. Its shape and size are the cypsela's. Ratios such as 'carpopodium 1/4 as long as achene body' use pattern 10 with the cypsela as the second part.

target: leaflet apex (FLOPO_0986000)
reason: Narrower: pinna is a PO synonym of leaflet, so the apex of a pinna is a leaflet apex. The spinulose and spinescent examples point to cycads.

target: scale leaf (PO_0006003) part of short shoot (PO_0004701)
reason: In Pinus, the sheath of bud scales (cataphylls) round the base of a needle fascicle, which is a short shoot. A collective of scale leaves, so the existing classes express it. 'fascicle' alone was rejected as generic.

Ambiguous without context: the word is used for blister-like leaf swellings, which are a quality (bullate FLOPO_0991122), and in some taxa for a discrete swelling on another organ. I couldn't tell which taxon or organ the rhomboid, plano-convex bullae 2-3 mm in diameter belong to.

target: lamina (PO_0025060) part of leaf rachis (PO_0020055)
reason: A laminar extension of a winged leaf rachis (e.g. Sapindaceae), modelled exactly on petiole lamina PO_0025129 ('petiole wing'), which PO defines as a lamina part of a petiole. 'wing' alone was rejected as needing its organ.

target: calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005) at fruit development stage (PO_0001002), pattern 04
reason: An existing FLOPO class in the fruiting state. 'fruiting' is a stage context word.

Ambiguous: 'seed chamber' can mean a fruit locule (PO_0025270, a cavity), the seed-bearing body of a samara, or a segment of a pod. The qualities (ovoid, prickly, rugose, 4-6 cm long) describe a solid seed-bearing part of a fruit, which none of these fits without the taxon.
